abstract: Morgan Stanley's AlphaWise survey of 935 corporate executives across the US, Germany, Japan, and Australia finds that companies in five AI-exposed sectors reported an 11.5% increase in net productivity and a 4% net decline in headcount over the past 12 months. AI adoption led to elimination of 11% of jobs, with an additional 12% left unfilled, partially offset by 18% new hires. US companies were an outlier, reporting a 2% net job gain.
keyFindings: 4% net global headcount decline: 11% eliminated + 12% unfilled - 18% new hires across 5 sectors
US companies reported 2% net job gain; UK saw 8% net loss; Germany 4% net loss
11.5% average net productivity increase across all countries and sectors
Automotive sector had highest net job loss at 10%; real estate saw 1% net gain
Larger firms (501-1,000 employees) cut 15% of positions; small firms (<49) gained 4%
Early-career positions most at risk: highest rates of elimination without replacement
27% of employees retrained in past 12 months
methodology: AlphaWise survey of 935 corporate executives in the US, Germany, Japan, and Australia. Five sectors: consumer staples distribution & retail, real estate management & development, transportation, healthcare equipment & services, and automobiles & components. Companies had been using AI for at least one year.
qualifiers: Results likely represent the worst-case scenario for workforce impact, as the survey focused on 5 sectors deemed most exposed to AI. US-specific results showed net job creation, not loss. Stephen Byrd noted: 'Although the results likely represent the worst-case scenario for workforce impact, the data provide an early warning about the potential negative effects on employment as AI technology continues to rapidly improve.'
